provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation:
The original task splits a 12x4 input into two stacked 6x4 halves along the rows. One half uses colour 3 and the other uses colour 5, both on background 0. The output is the cell-wise OR of the two halves, painted in colour 4.

Under D4, the optional row reversal (indices >= 4) only mirrors each half within itself. It does not change which axis separates the two halves. An odd number of clockwise rotations turns the stacked halves into side-by-side halves. So the emitted program splits along columns when d4 % 4 is odd and along rows when it is even.

Rotation and reflection may swap the two halves or mirror them, but both halves are moved the same way. Because OR is symmetric and works cell by cell, the result lines up exactly with the transformed output.

Colour roles are fixed as constants: background = palette[0] and output ink = palette[4]. Any cell in either half that is not background becomes ink. This also avoids relying on the specific half colours palette[3] and palette[5]. The program works directly in visible coordinates and never undoes the rotation or remaps colours.
draft_notes.limitations:
- The program assumes the split dimension has even length, which matches the constructor (it always builds a height of 2*6). If that dimension were odd, the middle line would be ignored.
- The demonstrations are not consulted, because the split axis and colour roles are fully determined by d4 and palette.
- I found no constructor defects or fixture contradictions. The fixtures match the uniform OR rule, and the generator has no tie-breaks or indexing quirks. (The bottom docstring says 'top grid', but this is only a comment typo.)
- I have not run any tests on this factory.

independent_source_review.mechanism: The input is two equal halves stacked along one axis: the first half uses palette[3] and the second uses palette[5], both on a palette[0] background. The output is the cell-wise OR of the two halves, painted in palette[4]. Under D4 augmentation the stacking axis becomes columns exactly when the number of quarter-turns (d4 % 4) is odd. The emitted solver splits along the visible axis and paints INK wherever either half is not BG.
evidence: Constructor: grid rows 0..height-1 hold 3 where top[i] is set, and rows height..2*height-1 hold 5 where bottom[i] is set. The output expression is `4 if top[i] + bottom[i] >= 1 else 0`, which is a pure cell-wise OR. There are no ties, no tie-breaks and no hidden latents beyond the visible bits.

Random path: top and bottom are independent per-cell randint(0,1) draws with fixed width 4 and height 6. The doubled dimension is always 12, so it is even and `g.shape[axis]//2` splits exactly with no ignored middle line.

All four approved train fixtures and the test fixture are generated by validate() through the same generate() call. I hand-checked train pair 1 row 0 (3300 | 0500 -> 4400) and test row 2 (0003 | 0050 -> 0044), and both agree with the OR rule.

Axis logic: every D4 element can be written as a reflection (or identity) composed with rot^k. Width and height are swapped iff k is odd, whichever flip axis the reflection uses. So `axis = 1 if k%2==1 else 0` correctly finds the visible split. Both halves undergo the same transform and OR is symmetric, so a swapped or mirrored half order still gives the correctly transformed output.

The solver works directly in augmented visible coordinates using the slices g[:h], g[h:2h] or g[:, :w], g[:, w:2w]. The output shape is first.shape, which matches the transformed 6x4 or 4x6 output. There is no untransform/solve/retransform wrapper.

Colours: BG = palette[0] and INK = palette[4]. The test `!= BG` covers palette[3] and palette[5] without needing to know which half has which colour. The ink colour 4 is a constant role that every demonstration output shows, so it is not an arbitrary association that needs extra evidence. d19f7514 is not in the episode_evidence_checks list, which is consistent with this.
Host audit passed: 1000 fresh pairs, 8000 augmented checks, 16 fixture variants, no sampler rejections.
nonblocking_limits: The solver ignores the demonstrations. This is acceptable because the split axis and colour roles are fully determined by d4 and palette.
If the split dimension were odd, the middle line would be ignored. This is out of domain, because the constructor always builds 2*height = 12.
The constructor docstring for `bottom` says 'top grid'. This is a comment typo only and does not affect behaviour.
Calling generate() with top supplied but bottom=None would fail. This path is unreachable in both the random path and validate().
required_context_checks: Confirm that the host's D4 indexing composes a reflection with rot^(d4%4), so that odd d4%4 means axes are swapped. The passing 8000 augmented checks with d4=7 support this.
